label: Bible Study
prompt: For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the _____.
verse: For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly.
note: Christ didn't wait for us to get strong — he died for the ungodly.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And I will make them and the places round about my hill a blessing; and I will cause the shower to come down in his _____; there shall be showers of blessing.
verse: And I will make them and the places round about my hill a blessing; and I will cause the shower to come down in his season; there shall be showers of blessing.
note: Rain right on schedule — 'showers of blessing,' a phrase that later became the title of a well-loved hymn.

label: Sunday School
prompt: I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and _____ write unto thee:
verse: I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and pen write unto thee:
note: John had more to say but preferred talking face to face over ink and pen.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to the LORD, but to the _____.
verse: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to the LORD, but to the physicians.
note: Asa had trusted God against a million-man army — but late in life he trusted doctors, not the LORD.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will _____ purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
verse: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
note: Not a typo: 'throughly' is the KJV's old form of thoroughly. John the Baptist's winnowing fan leaves nothing unsifted.
